resources.string: SailDash: split screen

SailDash uses this service only to put two apps side by side (split screen) when you tap Split or open your map or music. It doesn\'t read the screen, doesn\'t see what you type and doesn\'t save anything.
Map on the left and music on the right, each in its own half. A Split button appears in the side bar.
This head unit runs Android %1$s: two apps side by side needs Android 7 or newer.
Your head unit comes with two apps side by side turned off. Sometimes you can turn it on in Developer options with “Force activities to be resizable” (and restarting the head unit).
Also when you tap a map or your music
When you open them from SailDash, their partner opens in the other half (in landscape). Turn this off to split only with the button.
Accessibility service
On: SailDash can split the screen.
Off: turn on “SailDash: split screen” in Accessibility.
It\'s on, but Android hasn\'t connected it yet. If it stays like this, turn it off and on again.
Open Accessibility

On Android 7 an app can only split the screen through an accessibility service. SailDash uses it just for that: it doesn\'t read the screen or what you type, and it turns itself off if you turn split screen off.
Left half
Right half
None of the known apps is installed: find another one with “Other app…”.
Try it
Drag the middle bar to resize; push it to an edge to keep just one app.
An app won\'t split? In Developer options turn on “Force activities to be resizable” and restart the head unit.
Split
Turn on the service
To put two apps side by side, turn on “SailDash: split screen” in Android\'s Accessibility settings. SailDash uses it only to split: it doesn\'t read the screen.
Choose the apps
Choose the app for each half in Settings → Apps → Split screen.
Close

Couldn\'t split the screen with %1$s. If that app won\'t allow it, see the tip in Settings → Apps → Split screen.
To open in split screen, turn on “SailDash: split screen” in Accessibility.
